h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, מַאֲמָר י״א Rosh Chodesh Adar — Maamar Yud Aleph

p: in the order of the banners,
and it emerges that Adar is for Naftali.
And this is what it says in Sefer Yetzirah:
"He crowned the letter Kuf in laughter";
for of Naftali it is written (Devarim 33:23),
and as the Raavad also wrote,
that laughter is for Naftali for this reason
"and full of the blessing of Hashem";
"The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich,"
of the wise and the foolish in words of Torah.
"The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich" —
to merit the wealth of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
And this is what it says (Devarim ibid.),
in the manner of what it says (Tehillim 21:3),
"The desire of his heart You have given him,
and the request of his lips You have not withheld, Selah";
"When have You given him the desire of his heart?
When the request of his lips
And this is what it says (Devarim ibid.),
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
and he is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
וְדָרוֹם כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and "south" corresponds to Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
to bring down the light of Torah,
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham";
in the utterance "Let there be light"
correspond to the Five Books of the Torah
and with Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
הָיָה הַכֹּל בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
everything was in the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
and his father did not teach him;
and this is like Torah she'b'al peh:
"My words which I have placed in your mouth"
in the heart of the sages.
And this is what he said, "yerashah":
for not all the tribe were talmidei chachamim,
in the manner of what they said (Devarim 33:4),
"an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov,"
a portion in words of Torah.
And this is what it says, "yerashah":
like an inheritance, which has no interruption
וּבִרְכַּת נַפְתָּלִי מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And Naftali's blessing from Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רלד, ב)
"and you shall say in your heart";
Hashem Yisbarach causes to shine forth
in the heart of the sages.
"Beautiful," in the manner of what they said
resembled two orbs of the sun;
so that he is as before the corruption
(as stated in Beshalach, beginning of maamar 4);
and this is "who gives beautiful words":
in the answer of his mouth...";
When the answer is in his mouth."
which alludes to Alef, the supernal Wonder,
Yud, which shines forth from the root
for the Hei was a Dalet,
and once it became impregnated with the Yud, as is known;
Shin is the secret of the three Avos
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
that is, he merits the holiness of Shabbos,
for the daughter is crowned with the Avos;
for then is the time to merit
And it is written, "Naftali is a hind let loose";
in its plain sense, that he ran like a hind,
that they sent him to Mitzrayim
to bring the deed of sale from Mitzrayim.
But the Torah does not mention as praise
rather the main praise is in words of Torah,
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem";
וּבָזֶה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין לָהֶם מְנוּחָה
and in this, talmidei chachamim have no rest,
לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
neither in this world nor in the World to Come
and a person would want to run
the leaven in the dough holds him back
and in the future they will go from strength to strength;
and "Naftali is a hind let loose":
that he merits to go from strength to strength,
as it will be in the future.
and this is the holiness of this month:
to merit the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
which corresponds to the holiness of Naftali,
And in the sefer Kedushas Levi
he counted the month of Adar against Yosef,
וְעַל כֵּן מִתְחַלֵּק בִּשְׁנַת הָעִיבּוּר לִשְׁנַיִם
and therefore it divides in two in a leap year,
(as explained in maamar 10; see there at length);
who brought Yisrael into Eretz Yisrael,
which is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
as we said (in the previous maamar)
for it is the arrangement of Eretz Yisrael."
And afterward from his seed will come
who will gather the dispersed of Yisrael
עַל יְדֵי אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
through the light of Torah she'b'al peh

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 10 — “Torah she'b'al peh has levels, and one must learn it from another, unlike the Written Torah … Hashem provided his two kidneys like two teachers… this language too alludes only to Torah she'b'al peh.” Rav Tzadok explains why Avraham's Torah counts as Oral Torah. It grew from within him rather than from a written text, and so it belongs to Malchus, the “bas” the Zohar says was given to Avraham.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 61:1 — “Rabbi Shimon said: His father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where did Avraham learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, provided his two kidneys as two teachers, and they flowed and taught him Torah and wisdom, as it is written, I shall bless Hashem, who counseled me; even at night my kidneys instructed me.” The Midrash offers several accounts of Avraham's Torah knowledge. This teaching emphasizes inward Divine instruction rather than an inherited human teaching chain.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Nasso 5637 (1877), s.v. BeAvos Moshe Kibel Torah — “Although Torah was given to all Israel, there are two aspects of Torah. One is the toil through which every Jew can find something in Torah, each according to his grasp. There is also a special property of Torah through which the sages who lead the generations attain what does not follow from human reasoning. This is the inheritance given us, as it says, 'Moshe commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.' … The Gemara says: 'Do not read morashah, inheritance, but me'orasah, betrothed.' The distinction is that an inheritance comes without toil, an inheritance that has no interruption; betrothal is a closeness attained through a person's actions and toil in Torah. It is to each individual that the instruction applies: 'Prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you.' Of Israel collectively it says, 'an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.' Nevertheless, by meriting to include himself within the whole of Israel, a person also merits a share in the inheritance.”

rich.text: Parallel:
R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Nasso 5637 (1877), s.v. BeAvos Moshe Kibel Torah

— “Although Torah was given to all Israel, there are two aspects of Torah. One is the toil through which every Jew can find something in Torah, each according to his grasp. There is also a special property of Torah through which the sages who lead the generations attain what does not follow from human reasoning. This is the inheritance given us, as it says, 'Moshe commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.' … The Gemara says: 'Do not read morashah, inheritance, but me'orasah, betrothed.' The distinction is that an inheritance comes without toil, an inheritance that has no interruption; betrothal is a closeness attained through a person's actions and toil in Torah. It is to each individual that the instruction applies: 'Prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you.' Of Israel collectively it says, 'an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.' Nevertheless, by meriting to include himself within the whole of Israel, a person also merits a share in the inheritance.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: This distinction qualifies the meaning of a share available to every Jew. The inheritance belongs enduringly to Israel as a whole, while the individual's developed grasp still calls for toil and differs from person to person. Sefat Emet thus explains how a universal, uninterrupted inheritance can coexist with the Mishnah's warning that Torah is not simply inherited by an individual. This illuminates Rav Tzadok's express qualification that not every member of the tribe was a scholar, although each has a portion.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 129b — “Rav Acha son of Rav Avya sent: According to Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah, if one says, My property is yours, and after you, so-and-so's, and the first recipient is fit to inherit him, the second has nothing in place of the first. This is not the language of a gift but the language of inheritance, and inheritance has no interruption.” The legal rule concerns inherited property. Rav Tzadok uses its language to illuminate Torah as the enduring inheritance of Israel.

paragraphs.text: ZoharI 234b, Vayechi 53, s.v. Vayomer — “And he said: what is meant by And he said? We have established it, as Scripture says, You shall say in your heart: saying in silence. Gather yourselves: it should have said Gather! Rather, Gather yourselves comes from above: gather in a complete bond, in a single unity. And I shall tell you is the mystery of wisdom.” Rav Tzadok draws specifically on saying in silence to explain Oral Torah appearing within the sages' hearts.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rav Tzadok HaKohen, Resisei Layla 6:2 — “Prayer's essence is a broken heart. ... A broken heart is the opposite of joy: when a person considers his particular deficiencies and the great salvation and mercy he needs, reason would say that sadness and worry should fill him. But God's commandments work oppositely: they give birth to joy, and this is the sign that prayer is complete and accepted. Words of Torah in themselves gladden the heart. ... When study is for its own sake, the sign is that it gives birth instead to reverence and care, as they said: Great is study, for it leads to action.”

paragraphs.text: Sotah 13a — “They said: Who shall go? Let Naftali go, for he is as swift as a hind, as it is written, Naftali is a hind sent forth, who gives beautiful words. Rabbi Abahu said: Do not read beautiful words, but beautiful documents.” The documents concern Esav's sale of his share in the burial place. The narrative is the concrete background for Naftali's speed and the words/documents wordplay.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ha'azinu 6 — “The tzaddikim will go from strength to strength… from Shabbos to Shabbos … and there is no satiation in Torah except through Shabbos, which is a semblance of the future.” Rav Tzadok answers the Maharsha's question on Berachos 64a. The future has rest only from the yetzer, never from ascent, and Shabbos already gives a taste of that ceaseless ascent.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 3 — “They will merit to bring out the nine kabin of wisdom of Eretz Yisrael that were captive … all the exiles are for this… Had they merited, Yehoshua would have been Mashiach ben Yosef.” This shows how Torah she'b'al peh will repair everything. Yosef's line, from Yehoshua to Mashiach ben Yosef, has the task of gathering the wisdom scattered among the nations, and that is the purpose of the exiles.
